articleTitle: Remote laboratories for electrical & electronic subjects in new engineering grades
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper discusses a new technology for making electric and electronic circuit experiments remotely. Virtual Instrument System in Reality (VISIR) has been implemented at the Spanish University for Distance Education (UNED) for new engineering grade's distance laboratories. It gives a brief update of the project and its implementation, on the other hand, discusses its role at the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department at UNED.

articleTitle: A web-based tool for a Power Electronics course
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents a computer-aided educational package for the study of Power Electronics. This work is framed within the guidelines established by the European Higher Education Area, which promotes the active role of the students. The software includes: a dynamic and interactive tool for simulating steady-state ideal power electronics converters, multimedia resources as video animations of operation of power electronics circuits and self-evaluation test automatically corrected and graded by the software. The software provided highly favorable results when compared with students who did not use it.

articleTitle: A review of teaching power system harmonics
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: One of the main aspects of power quality is harmonic related problems in power systems. A proper learning of harmonics is essential for power engineers to deal with these problems. This paper reviews the efforts made in teaching power system harmonics in undergraduate and graduate levels. Hardware and software tools have been developed in order to improve the teaching/learning process. General aspects of these tools are presented, as well as their educational methodologies. Conclusions, improvement ideas and future work lines are also launched.

Author Keywords: power system harmonics and power quality

articleTitle: Code of good practice in teaching - Process map
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Both the society at large institutions, are suing the university system in compliance with quality requirements. The group EduQTech, university R & D + i whose main objective is the application of the concepts of quality in R & D in university teaching, has proposed the development of a Code of Practice-based Teaching quality criteria and can be applied to a Masters course or degree, a self-study or specialization course. This paper aims to present the first steps are being taken to the preparation of the Code of Practice, ie the development of a process map.

articleTitle: Repository of good practices applied to higher education in engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The aim of the repository is to provide resources obtained from the analysis of good practices, to improve the processes of competency-based training in engineering degrees. To do this, we have analyzed over 800 cases and obtained methodologies, techniques, resources and tools applicable in the university training context. The project organizes, classifies and facilitates the searching of those good practices using the search engine 2.0.

articleTitle: Development of an integrated virtual-remote lab for teaching induction motor starting methods
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a integrated virtual/remote lab for teaching induction motor starting methods used in the Civil Engineering School at the Polytechnic University of Madrid.

articleTitle: Educational activities and results obtained from a University-Industry collaborative framework experience
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Collaboration between Industry and University is becoming more important in order to improve the competitiveness of the research and development activities. Moreover, establishing synergies to bridge the gap between the academic and industrial spheres has demonstrated to be advantageous for both of them. Nowadays, Industry is moving towards an open innovation structure, in which external agents as universities play a key role. Besides, University is also seeking a more active learning methodology to improve the education of students for the real world. Considering this framework, a special effort should be done to take advantage of the collaborative work between Industry and University. The aim of this paper is to present the collaborative framework and the benefits obtained of the educational activities as a consequence of the long-term collaboration established between the University of Zaragoza and the Bosch and Siemens Home Appliances Group. The key stones of the collaboration are presented, and the positive outcomes for the students are highlighted. The strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of the proposed program are also discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement of the time of study
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper we try to present the results of a study about the time devoted by students to learn every subject in an Electrical Engineering Degree in accordance with the Bologna process. A survey during two years has been done to the students of Electrical Engineering Diploma in the School of Engineers of the University of Zaragoza. Some results are presented in the paper and a particular analysis for two subject in the first and in the third year has been done.

articleTitle: Peer to peer evaluation - Methodology and experiences across moodle platform
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Teacher works as evaluator in his day by day, and very often, this job is based on exams correction. Traditional exams have been fundamental, but present a problem: students are not connected with evaluation process. Otherwise, peer to peer evaluation is based on the role of students as evaluators: they have to know and assume evaluation criteria and applying them on other exams. With this, students are able to understand better the contents, and develop skills to qualify his partners. Then, teacher could define evaluation grades: numeric, byelements presence, by rubrics... And at last, only has to define a schedule for leaving works, evaluating and to generate the final qualification. This paper shows experiences using peer to peer evaluation across Moodie platform on two academic courses.

articleTitle: An approach on how to use audiovisual resources at Engineering Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper an approach to the use of audiovisual material (AM) is presented as an important resource for university education. Some AM has been created, which not only has been used in laboratory and master lecturing but also it has helped us in the task of increasing the efficiency of teaching. This work intends to show some examples of production and use of AM for university education.

articleTitle: Blended learning (b-learning) in telecommunications engineering - A study case
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Blended learning (b-learning) in higher education is facilitated by the effective combination of different modes of delivery, models of teaching and styles of learning. Moreover, it is based on transparent communication amongst students and teachers. This paper shows how the Course Management System (CMS), Moodle, can assist a teacher at a School of Telecommunications Engineering to create a b-learning environment. Moreover, this platform can be used by teachers to provide online content and activities to their students and it facilitates the student learning.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of a mentoring program in the computer science degrees at the Universitat Politecnica de Valencia - Impact of the PATU program at the Escuela Tecnica Superior de Ingenieria Informatica of the UPV
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this work we show the impact of a mentoring program for freshmen set for the degrees taught at the Escuela Tecnica Superior de Ingenierlia Informatica of the Universitat Politecnica de Valencia. We analyze the variables that influence the student participation in the program, and we evaluate the impact that following up it has for an improvement of the academic performance of the students.

articleTitle: Cloud-based architecture for e-leaming
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents our work on the developement of an architecture for e-learning that is based on cloud computing. This includes the creation of virtualized environments to be used in the field of networks and communications, and the development of techniques to predict the load of the technology infrastructures of the university. The main aim of this work is to improve the use of the resources of the technology infrastructure of the university and provide an easy to use environment for students.

articleTitle: Off-campus problem-based learning: approach in paper or computer-assisted? - A experience in atmospheric pollution
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Off-campus activities have taken on special importance in the new context of the non-contact teaching of engineering. This study investigates the effectiveness of several educational materials for problem-based learning in an Aerospace Engineering degree offered at Polytechnic University of Valencia. The activities based on the use of paper documents were compared to exercises performed through educational platforms with specific multimedia material or obtained from the Internet. The comparison criteria are the ability to solve professional cases, the development of skills associated with selective information search and the acquisition of scientific-technical language. It was concluded that the learning outcoming,student satisfaction and used time depends on both the format (paper or electronic) and the type of activity. The use of computer provides best results for open-questions or activities of information seeking.

articleTitle: Co-evaluation ICT techniques applied to an integrated project for new degrees in Spain
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this work, a set of Information and Technology based tools are presented. These techniques are designed to improve the development of an Integrated Project to be used in the new Bachelor Degree of Mechanical Engineering in Spain. A method of peer-review is proposed which is intended to offer the professor a wider point of view over the student learning process. Furthermore, this method will make the student to get involved in the evaluation process.

articleTitle: Pre-laboratory self-assessment by e-learning platform poliformat - A multidisciplinar experience
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the implementation of pre-laboratory questionnaires in different subjects taught in technical degrees. We studied the main variables for the design and application through e-learning platform. This type of questionnaire allows each student assessing his/her knowledge before a practical session. It promotes student interest and thus, better use of resources. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy has been established from qualitative and quantitative data collected through observation, marks and a specific poll. Finally,the comparative analysis of several disciplines showed the advantages and disadvantages of this strategy and the key points for extrapolating these teaching-learning activities to any university subject.

articleTitle: Design tools and control activities in the field of Engineering Graphics
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper reflects the experience gained over the last two years in the implementation of different teaching activities, exercises/ practices/ controls (EPC), in subjects in the area of Graphic Engineering, since its approach to evaluation. It is based on the use of two basic tools software for parametric design and Athena platform, developed in Moodle LMS for its managent.

articleTitle: Process management applied to improving a subject of graphic engineering efficiency indicators and monitoring
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This work includes a proposed methodology oriented integrated management of materials and subjects. The approach is based on technical analysis and treatment process. Has been adopted as experimental material the subject of Graphic Expression in Engineering, which is a core course common to different studies degree in engineering. Finally, we provide a number of proposals and recommendations on possible qualitative and quantitative indicators suitable for assessing the quality of other subjects.

articleTitle: Teaching methodology based on role playing games - A comparison of organizational alternatives in the management of warehouse logistics
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: A teaching methodology for learning "by doing" is proposed, where each participant plays a role to simulate different organizational configurations of picking in a finished product warehouse. The pooling of results complemented with the presentation of good practice enables the effectiveness of the learning process in a four hours workshop. This methodology is appropriate for university teaching.

articleTitle: Promoting mathematical skills using the instructive program Kriging
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Geostatistics was developed in mining for the grade estimation problems of ore deposits, nowadays; it is the most popular method for the interpolation and estimation problems. Methodological consideration about its interpolator, the Kriging, is presented in this paper. For geosciences engineering and other students in general is important to take in advance interpolation methods. This methodology is coming from natural phenomenon, where it is very difficult or even impossible to build deterministic models, only it is possible to describing the behavior from fragmented information of the problem studied. The characterization of the spatial variables using geostatistics has, in general, two main steep: the structural analysis to obtain semivariogram models and the estimation by Kriging. The solution of the problems using Kriging program allows to promoting mathematical skills in the students when they apply the methodology to classroom and real case studies and has to take decisions.

articleTitle: HyBook: A lifelong learning management system in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents HyBook, an ad-hoc tool which was designed and implemented with the objective of improving the workflow management, and to allow the possibility of automatically generating e-books regarding educational courses at the Instituto de Ciencias de la Educaciòn (ICE) of the Universidad de Zaragoza (UZ). So far, when the ICE of the UZ wanted to start a new educational initiative, the usual elaboration process of the informative resources was performed manually. Now, by using our application the ICE will be able to centralize the information collection process, and automatically create the two leaflets that the ICE publishes each year in a more simply and conveniently way.

articleTitle: Active methodologies in the Quantitative Methods II course belonging to Industrial Management Engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: It is shown the adaptation performed in the Quantitative Methods II course, belonging to Industrial Management Engineering taught in the Polytechnic University of Valencia, Spain with the aim of incorporating a educational methodology in line with the European Higher Education Area.

Author Keywords: Palabras clave- Adaptacion de asignaturas al marco del Espacio Europeo de Educacion Superior

articleTitle: Making attractive business administration education in engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This document provides some ideas and guidelines to follow for the students of industrial engineering electronics that demostrate interest in the subject of business administration and production organization.

articleTitle: An experience of continuous assessment in ETSIT: new costs for the teacher
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents a proposal for continuous assessment in a subject of the first course in Telecommunications Technology Engineering. It describes the methodology itself, implementation experience and feedback from students about it. The paper concludes with an analysis on the cost for the teacher of the implementation of such techniques of continuous assessment.

articleTitle: Automatic test assessment web platform
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) is an on-line University. The UOC offers student-centered learning. Therefore, the UOC supports continuous evaluation throughthe courses. Thanks to the continuous exercises, students receive feedback about their progress during the semester. However, the UOC has a high number of students. The correction of the exercises is manual, thus teachers have to dedicate too much time to correct them. In this scenario, the UOC proposes an automatic evaluation tool that allows the student to evaluate himself anytime and receive instant feedback. This tool is a web-based platform and it intends to provide with flexibility both to students, by allowing to test their skills at any given moment, and teachers, by reducing the workload of their correction and feedback tasks. It has to be noticed that this tool has been designed for engineering subjects. Therefore, this tool is prepared to work with math symbols and formulas. The automatic test assessment is based on latent semantic indexing techniques.

articleTitle: Experience of using a evaluation system based on learning portfolios
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper describes the teaching experience applied to a subject in the Master of Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency at the University of Zaragoza. This experiment consisted of implementing a new system of continuous evaluation based on the presentation of a portfolio and the development of a subject project.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a training tool simulator as an educational resource in Digital Systems Fundamentals
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In introductory courses on Digital System Fundamentals, it seems difficult to deal with all the circuits presented in the classroom, from a practical perspective. In order to reinforce the learning outcomes of the course and, based on the commercial trainer tool DET 2020, this paper describes the design and implementation of a simulation tool that resembles the commercial training tool, and its use as educational resource in a first-year course in Computer Engineering. We present the educational possibilities of this powerful tool, both from the student and the instructor perspective, and we discuss the results of the students' assessment about the simulator.

articleTitle: AUTOGRAF: An educational tool with GRAFCET syntax controller - Constructivist approach for "digital devices for industrial automation"
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This work presents the design and implementation of an educational tool for teaching Grafcet language and its use in the subject "Digital Devices for Industrial Automation."

articleTitle: Short term activities in industrial informatics
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This document describes the preparation and implementation of online educational activities in Industrial Informatics subject taught in the Industrial Engineering degree specializing in Industrial Electronics, where two tutors teach. The course lasts two semesters. One professor teaches in the first half and another in the second. The activities are implemented in the second semester. This document describes the motivation, preparation and difficulties encountered in the design of activities, the feedback received by students and the software used. The natural environment where these actions take place is the web. The examples showed here can be accessed online. As a work in progress, the results should be considered estimated and are presented in this article as experience.

articleTitle: Non presential supporting plan for learners who have failed a subject
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper it is presented a supporting plan for learners who do not have the possibility of develop a subject in presential format. Instructional design tries to provide the basis for improving the learner's achievement. The proposal is compatible with European Space of Superior Education (EEES) applied to engineering learning programs.

articleTitle: Support planning to the implementation of School of Engineering in Computer Science - An oriented approach to teacher training
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Main objective of Action Plan for European Convergence (PACE) that Universitat Politecnica de Valencia (UPV) has been developing since academic year 2005-2006 has been to facilitate the process of adaptation of new courses of bachelor's degree to the European Higher Education Area (EEES). To carry out this ambitious project, centers have identified a set of coordinated actions by teams of teachers interested in teaching innovation. One of the activities promoted by School of Engineering in Computer Science (ETSINF) of UPV is a training plan for teachers. The main objective is to provide teachers with tools that facilitate the design of new courses of Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering under the current regulations, with particular emphasis on two aspects: the use of active methodologies and the evaluation criteria. This article describes the training activities that have taken place in the ETSINF during academic year 2009-2010 and the results of opinion poll for teachers about the appropriateness of these actions and their impact on the process to adapt their courses.

articleTitle: Software simulation platform for learning techniques for identifying kinematic parameters of industrial robots
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation software of capture and analysis of data for parameter identification of robot kinematic models developed for learning the discipline and the practical sessions under the activity for courses for master and postgraduate students adapted to the EHEA. After the content of the theoretical sessions, the software will be used for practical sessions, from a constructivist approach, encouraging independent learning of the students. This parametric software covers most important aspects of a robot calibration procedure and the influences on accuracy: 1) kinematic modeling, 2) data capture procedure, 3) parameter identification methods, 4) evaluation of the calibration. Also it allows to understand how each influence spreads to the final error and how to minimize sources of error in the process to establish optimal conditions for the highest possible accuracy in the parameters identified.

articleTitle: Adaptation of the course "Statistics" to the bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: With the introduction of the new four-year Degree in Engineering for its integration in the European Higher Education Area (EHEA), the challenge is to adapt existing courses to the requirements of the new curricula. In this work, we report the case of the course of Statistics in the Degree in Computer Engineering at the Polytechnic University of Valencia (UPV), with emphasis on the problems encountered and the proposed solutions.

articleTitle: Assessment of basic competences in Computing degrees at the UPM
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The assessment of the basic and general transferable competences defined by the Decree 1393/2007, (BOE num. 260, October 30th 2007), where official higher education is regulated, is a task that every university must deal with for a further evaluation of the ANECA in order to keep their degrees' accreditation. In this paper we will show the procedure we have designed and run in order to evaluate such competences in three degrees of the Technical University of Madrid (UPM), all of them related with Computing: Computer Engineering Degree, Software Engineering Degree and Computing Engineering Degree.

articleTitle: Design of e-activities and skills competencies in the field of Graphic Engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: It describes the methodology used in the design of e- activities to be performed by students outside the classrooms space, using different tools of a LMS (Moodle) and Web 2.0 as well as desirable skills in each case and evaluation.

articleTitle: MathemaTICs with ICT
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper we present some Learning Objects and Learning Modules that we have developed within the subjects of mathematics in the degree of architecture at the Universitat Politecnica de Valeincia and we present some results about our experience in introducing this type of digital material in the teaching-learning process of this discipline.

articleTitle: Cuadrics surfaces in the city of Valencia: DPGraph modeling
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper we present an experience we conducted at the Escuela Tecnica Superior de Arquitectura de Valencia. Our aim was double: 1) To promote the rapprochement between mathematics and architecture; and 2) To test the incorporation of DPGraph software as a teaching tool. The results were highly satisfactory in both directions, which led us to the conclusion of the use of DPGraph as a tool in computing practices of the mathematics subjects at the new degree in Architecture.

articleTitle: Implementation and first results of the Introduction to Engineering course in the ETSETB-UPC new degrees
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper describes the new course "Introduction to ICT Engineering" which has been conceived, designed and implemented at Telecom-BCN (ETSETB-UPC) from initial specifications and restrictions. It is the first of a series of four project subjects distributed throughout the new curricula. It is organized in three parallel paths covering the systemic vision of complex ICT systems, the basic concepts of economics, business and project management and the physical realization of a design-build project. In the first 5 years, this project is beling performed using the SeaPerch platform, a small underwater robot developed at MIT Sea Grant. A payload which includes measurement and communications subsystems is designed and built. After testing with small groups for two semesters, the course will be undertaken with around 250 students in the spring semester of this year.

articleTitle: Engineering projects performed under a model of hierarchical organization of students - Expertise and methodological innovation of teamwork
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The results of an innovative training experience carried out over several courses on engineering projects executed by student's teams, giving them a hierarchical organization structure are presented. This yields a stronger capacity for achieving more ambitious objectives and effectiveness. The paper addresses the problems and solutions that this hierarchical structure represents, along with how to implement guidelines for monitoring student's work, mentoring and specific assessment tasks that have been applied to Electronic Engineering projects.

articleTitle: Lessons learnt in using the TICs to improve teaching on Digital Systems Fundamentals
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The new scenario envisioned by the European Higher EducationArea (EHEA) seeks to enhance student participation in class, and to develop a proactive attitude towards their education. One priority aim of the Technical University of Valencia is to foster this attitude introducing a continuous assessment process. In this article, the lessons learnt in using the new Information and Communication Technologies (TICs) for teaching Digital Systems Fundamentals (GII-FCO) are presented. These technologies have been a key element in addressing this new approach, helping faculty in the assessment process.

articleTitle: Implementation of online prelab activities in introductory organic chemistry
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Over the last decades, the role of laboratory work in chemistry learning has shown a significant change. It is giving up its function as theoretical knowledge testing or simple experimental skills acquisition, to be integrated in methodologically coherent learning sequences. Taking into account the specificity of laboratory work concerning infrastructural and organizational issues, to achieve this goal requires the structuring activities introduction, such as the prelab tasks. These have turned out as very useful tools, whose communication new technologies. The aim of this paper is to show the process of implementation of a prelab activity model consisting of an audiovisual learning object which is linked to a multiple choice online test in an introductory organic chemistry course. The students' assessment has been clearly satisfactory, despite the work overload that it requires. Likewise, some results from this research show that the proposed prelab model may promote students' autonomy development and improve conceptual understanding, against the traditional "talk and chalk" way to laboratory work introduction.

articleTitle: Usage testing of game based learning in computer programming courses
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper describes the operation of a learning tool using the Game Based Learning (GBL) methodology. The developed tool, called e-Liza, operates as an activity from the e-learning platform Moodle. E-Liza allows us to pose question-response contests within individual or group games. This tool has been tested in several courses about programming languages undertaken in the Telecommunication Engineering Technical School, University of Valladolid, in the school year 2009-2010. In all the experiments performed, e-Liza has been well-accepted. The percentages of students passing the course who have used e-Liza application exceed the 80%. An important feature of the application is that it allows gathering a great number of statistical data from each student for each topic, showing a wide variety of graphs which can be used by the professor to evaluate the knowledge acquired by the students in any moment, and so, checking the extent of meeting the course objectives.

articleTitle: Remote and automatic evaluation in the EHEA for the network services
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to propose a remote system for the automatic evaluation of the activities related to a postgraduate subject. These activities imply the configuration of network services by using a virtual infrastructure. Our global framework is adapted to the EHEA; therefore, this system will be adapted to the students' learning requirements.

articleTitle: Adaptive instructional design of engineering online courses
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Online courses have been designed and experienced to support training in engineering mathematics through the generation of personalized itineraries. Adaptivity of these courses is based on prior knowledge of each student and his/her learning progress. We used the e-learning platform Moodle with Conditionals developed by the Innovation Centre for Information Society at the University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Here we present the design and results concerning the improvement in learning, user's satisfaction and lessons learned.

articleTitle: New collaboration tools applied to design teaching
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Collaborative design is identified within a technological strategy whereby tools and services over the internet permit designers to work in collaboration in order to develop and manage all the operations involved in the development process and life cycle of products. At a university level, teaching the use of collaboration tools has on the one hand centered on informing about the potential of the network for sharing and managing information about students in design projects that are becoming increasingly more multi-disciplinary and on the other hand applying technology to the internal philosophy in the exchange of geometrical information and Computer Aided Design programme data. The need to define and improve knowledge about development stages in industrial products will permit assessing the use of more optimum collaboration tools and applications in each design process generically and to further knowledge about the possibilities these tools have in the scope of promotion and communication with end users.

articleTitle: Cooperative learning in computer programming courses
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This paper presents a teaching method in use in the computer programming courses undertaken at the Telecommunication Engineering Technical School from the University of Valladolid. This method is based in the use of the cooperative learning. In particular, an adaptation of the jigsaw approach is proposed, including tournaments for verifying the learning process together with the parallel development of traditional programming practices, and a peer-reviewing process. Hence, in spite of the learning method being basically cooperative, both competitive inter-grouping and individual learning is used.

articleTitle: Using blogs in teaching postgraduate courses
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper we present the experience of using blogs in teaching postgraduate courses. For this, we previously describe good practices and principles that must be satisfied in order to determine whether the use of blogs allows achieving the main objective of teaching-learning process: the acquisition of skills by students. Finally, we show an example.

articleTitle: Teaching electromagnetic subject in electrical engineering degree at University of Granada (Spain)
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this work we present the educational innovations employed in adpating the subject "Wave Transmission" of the new Electrical Engineering Degree, which starts in September 2011 as an exigence from the knowledge society and the EU common policy for higher education. These innovations are based on a blended learning model which comprises both master classes and educational methods based on Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), by using the computational package Mathematica® and the Course Management System Moodle. The learning process is based on problem resolution and by following a text book. It is worth noting that the main subject syllabus has changed with the new plan, and that it is now structured in levels.

articleTitle: Fingerprint verification system in tests in moodle
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: This research describes the method of combining traditional authentication (password and username) with biometric technology, specifically fingerprint authentication. This authentication model is applied in distance education where courses are developed in learning management systems. It introduces the features of distance education as well as the biometric sensor operation. It describes the changes that are necessary to introduce in the learning management system in order to use the fingerprint as a data in the process of authentication. Finally, we performed tests of assessment the new authentication system in lab sessions at the college.

articleTitle: Computer Networks for Industrial Engineering by means of the PIGMALION method
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The design of a technical education course based on the application of the PIGMALION method, which includes the use of active methodologies for adaptation to the EHEA, is presented. Key aspects of the method are described, and accompanied by examples, like the definition of specific objectives, creating a detailed activities plan using a variety of objectives, creating a detailed activities plan using a variety of continuous assessment. In addition, the effort required by the teacher to adapt is outlined. Conclusions obtained in the first year of implementation include increased student motivation, and a significant improvement in the rate of return.

articleTitle: New teaching methodology for electronics and its adaptation to the European space for higher education
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: There is a widespread consensus that aims to the flexibility of the subjects, both in terms of times and places when and where they are taught as one of the main factors that increase or enhance their appeal for students. The deployment of a new remote access platform tailored to the specific needs of students in a course on digital electronic systems based on microprocessors has enabled them to enjoy greater flexibility by offering them the ability to complete remotely, in a different time and place to the university, the proposed practices (PBL) simultaneously with the lectures. This remarkable improvement, endorsed by the results of a survey among the students, has had a particularly positive impact on the impression students have of the subject, and has contributed significantly to improve its assessment and the participation in it.

articleTitle: University-Enterprise Educational models in Telecommunication Engineering Degree. The case of the Universidad Publica de Navarra in Spain.
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: The educational model for the degree, Master and Continuing Education in Telecommunication Engineering, centered in the capture of transverse competences, in order to offer an education model adapted to industry demands and the students involved. Experiences within the university degrees as well as in company education will be compared.

articleTitle: The adaptation to EHEA of a Natural Language Engineering course
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper we present a proposal to adapt the Natural Language Engineering course to the new European Higher Education Area. This adaptation is inspired upon three bases: the incorporation of the student as central element of the teaching-learning process, a detailed planning of attendance and non-attendance activities, and continuous assessment. The teaching methodology includes the definition of learning objectives of the course and their classification in three levels: knowledge, under-standing and application, the design of all activities for achieving them and the definition of a model of assessment at line with the proposed activities. Finally, we evaluate our experience and propose some improvements for subsequent courses.

articleTitle: Are Engineering students decreasing? Spain study case
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In Universities and other academic organizations have been saying that the number of students in Engineering masters and grades have been reduced. That means that fewer people will be working as engineers in the future. This is a fact that has alarmed Education Societies and Engineering Associations all over the world. Some reasons could be extracted from some loss of motivation when student looks at a difficult career, in spite of promising great labor expectations exposed from the Society. However, in this paper, some data are offered to change minds about this question, in particular in the case os Spain. Through the article, some figures have been used to get some conclusions in which demographic statistics, students' decisions and University published information could give an answer to the question, why do students demand other nonengineering careers? Is this true or just a myth?

articleTitle: Proposals for implementing a new degree on electronics and automation engineering
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: A new academic curriculum for the Electronics and Automation Enginering Degree at the University of Zaragoza, Spain has been developed in the contest of the European Space for Higher Education. We analyse the distribution and weight of basic contents (subjects related to Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Mechanics, Fluids...) and specialized contents (electronics and automation), pointing strengths and weaknesses. Finally, we propose some actions and methodologies for the implementation of this new academic curriculum, Intended to achieve a balance between basic and speclallsed contents oriented to educating Engineers for the European marker.

articleTitle: An application example to gain an insight into the electromagnetic quasistatic approach concept for graduate students
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: Quasistatic approach provides intermediate level of electromagnetic theory in between statics and the full set of Maxwell equations. This approach is introduced in the electrical engineering undergraduate courses due to its pedagogical significance. In standard textbooks, quasistatic approach refers to a regime where the system size is small with respect to the electromagnetic wavelength associated with the dominant sources. However, graduate students often find confusing issues concerning the applicability of this approach, especially in cases dealing with sources at medium-high frequencies and well removed from lossy or dissipative media. From an practical application example, a complementary perspective of classical quasistatic approach is proposed in this paper. This development was applied as rigorous justification of using quasistatic approach in some Ph.D. dissertations and it can also complement the contents appearing in textbooks used in electromagnetics teaching in postgraduate level courses.

articleTitle: Collaborative learning and videoconferences - Practical application in engineering studies
publicationTitle: 2011 Promotion and Innovation with New Technologies in Engineering Education (FINTDI 2011)
abstract: In this paper we present some experiences of working in collaborative environments in engineering studies. We also show the combined potential of those environments when involving the use of videoconferencing as a quality element in learning and as a simulation of professional work environments. The shown experiences have been applied in studies of Industrial Engineering and Aeronautical Engineering at Industrial and Aeronautical Engineering School of Terrassa (ETSEIAT).
